summary: The note surveys how solar storms and space weather affect modern infrastructure, using a series of 2023–2024 incidents and personal accounts. It covers power grid failures from geomagnetically induced currents, disruptions to GPS, internet, aviation and farming, and a community's response in Montague, Michigan. It closes by stressing efforts to build resilience through grid hardening, satellite shielding and better forecasting.
one_line: Overview of 2023–2024 solar storm incidents disrupting power grids, communications, aviation and agriculture, and the growing push for infrastructure resilience.
key_facts: On November 7, 2023, the sun expelled a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) that headed toward Earth and triggered alerts from space weather forecasters and utility companies.
Auroras from the November 2023 CME were visible as far south as Texas.
On November 9, 2023, Duluth, Minnesota lost power around seven-thirty in the evening when the town's grid succumbed to a geomagnetic induced current (GIC); it was about twenty degrees outside.

Dr. Emily Rios of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory said GICs create extra currents that can overload transformers and other critical infrastructure, calling it 'a silent tsunami for the electrical world.'
On September 23, 2023, a moderate solar storm disrupted satellite communications, including GPS and internet connectivity, across parts of North America.
Julian Torres, a freelance web designer in Denver, Colorado, missed a crucial deadline during the September 23, 2023 storm because he could not reach his team or online resources.
Polar flight routes save time and fuel but are extremely vulnerable to space weather events.
On September 28, 2023, Captain Hardeep Singh's flight near the Arctic Circle lost reliable communications and had to reroute for safety, causing delays and added airline costs.

Montague, Michigan suffered back-to-back power outages from severe solar storms in early March 2024; local businesses provided warmth and food and emergency services implemented a solar storm response plan.
On October 14, 2023, a solar flare incident caused GPS accuracy drops that temporarily stalled precision farming operations, affecting farmers such as Sarah Phillips of Iowa.
Resilience priorities include hardening electrical grids, improving satellite shielding, and developing more accurate space weather forecasting models.
